scripts/verify.nu FAIL branches print `verify: FAIL ...`, set $env.LAST_VERIFY_FAIL, and `return` — but nothing consumes LAST_VERIFY_FAIL and the script still exits 0 after a FAIL, despite the header's 'Exit 0 = all checks green' claim (rg confirms no consumer outside verify.nu). A caller relying on exit status alone would read a red verify as green; fix idea: `exit 1` on FAIL paths.

Narrowing is file-granular by design: an inline #[cfg(test)] module ADDED inside an existing src file is status M, so it runs the full crate suite (conservative over-run, not a gap) — only newly-added files qualify for the name-filter tier; noted so nobody reads the seed's 'purely-added' as covering inline additions to existing files.

painpoints.text: seed-spec-paths gate bounce (run 01M5CVG6XT9ABZFTMGY45QGCKT): the seed body names three loop-asset paths (implementer.md, planner.md, scripts/verify.nu) but the prior implementer pass shipped only two — the gate RED arrived only at tester time. Fix idea: surface the seed-spec-named path list in the implementer's own cheap lane (e.g. extend `nu scripts/qualitygate.nu check-run-scope loop` output or the claim_check stage payload to list spec-named paths vs current diff), so a missing unit part is caught before the tester cycle.

observations: Verified the narrowing's fail-safe edges directly in scripts/verify.nu (rename-status fallthrough to 'M', mixed added+edited crates forced to the full suite, empty-extraction disqualification, 0-tests-run fallback) — these are behaviors the green gate does not exercise.

test-fn-names resets its #[...] attribute window on any non-attribute line, so a blank line between #[test] and fn would drop that test from the name filter and the narrowed run could under-cover; bounded because the deterministic tester still runs the suites. A future seed could tighten the window to skip blank lines only.
